question.title: What will Magazine Luiza (MGLU3) close at on Friday, November 27, 2026?
question.description:
Magazine Luiza S.A. ("Magalu") is one of Brazil's largest retailers, listed on the B3 exchange under ticker MGLU3. Its shares trade in Brazilian reais (BRL) and are among the most heavily traded names on the exchange.

Status quo, as of the most recent completed session (Thursday, November 12, 2026): MGLU3 closed at R$7.07 after a violent week. It closed at R$5.84 on Nov 9, then rose 11.6% on Nov 10 (R$6.52), surged 17.5% on Nov 11 (R$7.66, intraday high R$7.82), and fell 7.7% on Nov 12 on 75.6M shares with a range of R$6.92–7.86. During Friday, November 13, it traded higher, in the R$7.1–7.6 area. That leaves the stock roughly 20–30% above its Nov 9 close, but still below its end-2025 close of R$8.94. The 52-week range is wide: R$3.76 to R$13.93 (the high was set as recently as September 2026). Market capitalization moved from roughly R$4.8bn to about R$6bn within a couple of sessions.

What is driving the move: (1) Third-quarter 2026 results, released Nov 9, showed net profit of R$13.9 million, down 34.4% year-on-year, but with signs of an operating turnaround — physical-store sales up 16% and own e-commerce up 14% in October, which commentary described as a possible inflection point. (2) A wave of sell-side revisions: Bank of America turned from underperform to buy with a R$11 target, and Goldman Sachs upgraded to buy on Nov 12, lifting its target from R$6.30 to R$11.50. JPMorgan, by contrast, kept its underweight rating, warning that a management proposal to authorise up to 1.55 billion new shares (about 200% of the current share base) — to be voted at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting (AGE) on December 2, 2026 — implies theoretical dilution of up to 67%. The LSEG consensus split was 5 buy / 5 hold / 2 sell with a mean 12-month target of R$9.43. (3) The distress of rival Casas Bahia was cited as a factor in the rally, on expectations of market-share gains. A heavily beaten-down stock, sharply conflicting sell-side views and a pending dilution vote have together produced two-sided moves of 7–17% per session, so a wide distribution is the sensible forecast rather than a point guess.

The forecast window: this question is forecast from around November 26, 2026, so the session being predicted is Friday, November 27, 2026 — the November 26 close (published the previous evening) is the last known price. Nov 27 is a normal B3 trading day and also Black Friday in Brazil (the day after US Thanksgiving), a key promotional date for Brazilian retailers; any same-day commentary on retail traffic or promotional intensity, plus positioning ahead of the December 2 shareholders' meeting on the share-authorisation proposal, are the live catalysts in that window.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the official B3 closing price of Magazine Luiza ON shares (ticker MGLU3) for the trading session of Friday, November 27, 2026, as shown in the "Close" column for the November 27, 2026 row on the Yahoo Finance historical data page for MGLU3.SA: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MGLU3.SA/history/ . Prices are in Brazilian reais, so a close of R$7.45 resolves as 7.45. If Yahoo Finance does not display a closing value for that session, the closing price reported for November 27, 2026 on the B3-sourced page https://www.cotab3.com.br/cotacao/MGLU3 will be used instead. If B3 holds no trading session on November 27, 2026, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: The "Close" column is used, not the "Adj Close" column (which is retroactively adjusted for dividends and corporate actions). Only the regular B3 session of November 27, 2026 counts; prices from any other session do not.
